title: The Quiet Floor
brief: 21:42, Zone 4 AutoStore grid. Three failed retrieval attempts in six minutes — no hard fault code, no stoppage. Every customer-facing dashboard reads green.
The change log shows a firmware push to that zone two hours earlier, ahead of peak-season load testing.

Right call: raise it as a Major Incident now. The criteria — needs another team, could reach a customer, has gone unresolved a while — don't wait for visible damage, and this already met one of the three.

drills.description_seed: Zone 4 showing intermittent retry faults following an unconfirmed firmware push, three days ahead of peak trading.
drills.escalation_brief: Four hours later, the same fault reaches Zone 5 — identical hardware, identical firmware, same fault pattern.
drills.worklog_seed: Firmware push confirmed as root cause. WMS Engineering paused the change platform-wide before it reached further zones.
drills.closure_comment_seed: Logged as a Major Incident at 21:50. Firmware push identified and paused before reaching Zone 5. Resolved ahead of the next shift.

title: Every Light at Once
brief: 21:45, Zones 2 and 3. Every unit alarms within the same ninety seconds — the floor display is a wall of red.
The maintenance calendar shows this exact pattern logged every Tuesday: a scheduled recalibration cycle, already clearing.
Right call: confirm against the calendar and stand down. Loud isn't the same as urgent — the criteria are about real signal, not how many lights are red.

drills.description_seed: Simultaneous fault alerts across Zones 2 and 3, cross-checked against the maintenance calendar.
drills.escalation_brief: A second wave of alerts clears exactly on schedule, confirming the calendar theory.
drills.worklog_seed: Confirmed against the maintenance calendar — scheduled recalibration, Zones 2 and 3. No fault found.
drills.closure_comment_seed: Zones 2 and 3 finished their scheduled cycle four minutes after the first alert, exactly as logged. Nothing about tonight was ever broken.
